cosponsors: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: Albania’s objectives are to condemn the Russian Federation’s aggression, demand immediate and unconditional withdrawal, reaffirm Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and ensure humanitarian access. We aim to secure at least nine votes and avoid a veto by holding the line on core principles, but the main difficulty is the anticipated Russian veto; if it is exercised, we will immediately pursue an emergency special session of the General Assembly. We also need to keep abstentionist members on board without weakening the text.

China.change: Delete the phrase “Condemns the Russian Federation’s aggression against Ukraine in violation of Article 2, paragraph 4, of the Charter” and replace it with: “Expresses grave concern at the ongoing military operations in Ukraine and calls on all parties to exercise maximum restraint and cease hostilities.”

Replace “Demands that the Russian Federation immediately cease its use of force against Ukraine and completely and unconditionally withdraw all of its military forces from the territory of Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders” with: “Calls upon all parties to immediately cease hostilities, pull back military forces from confrontation lines, and create conditions for political dialogue and negotiation.”

Replace “Deploring the declaration by the Russian Federation of a ‘special military operation’ in Ukraine” with: “Expressing grave concern at the declaration of a ‘special military operation’ and the ensuing military operations in Ukraine.”

Add: “Reaffirms that the legitimate security concerns of all countries should be respected, and calls for a settlement of the Ukraine crisis through dialogue and negotiation, including within the Normandy Format and on the basis of the Minsk agreements.”
Add “in accordance with humanitarian principles” after “humanitarian assistance for those in need”.

India.change: Delete the operative paragraph condemning 'the Russian Federation’s aggression against Ukraine' and replace it with: 'Expresses grave concern at the ongoing hostilities in and around Ukraine and calls upon all parties to immediately cease hostilities and return to dialogue and diplomacy.'

Replace 'Demands that the Russian Federation immediately cease its use of force against Ukraine and completely and unconditionally withdraw all of its military forces from the territory of Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders' with 'Calls upon all parties to immediately cease the use of force, de-escalate, and resolve differences through peaceful dialogue, consistent with the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of all States.'

Replace 'Deploring the declaration by the Russian Federation of a “special military operation” in Ukraine' with 'Expressing grave concern at the recent developments in and around Ukraine and the urgent need for de-escalation'.

Add: 'Calls for continued diplomatic efforts and supports negotiations in the Normandy Format and other formats aimed at a peaceful settlement, and encourages all parties to engage constructively in direct talks.'
Add at the end: ', and to ensure the safety and safe passage of civilians, including foreign nationals.'

Russian Federation.change: Delete: "Reaffirming the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders," or replace with a general reference to the purposes and principles of the Charter without singling out Ukraine's territorial integrity.

Delete: "Deploring the declaration by the Russian Federation of a “special military operation” in Ukraine," and replace with neutral language taking note of the deterioration of the situation in Ukraine.
Delete the entire paragraph: "Condemns the Russian Federation’s aggression against Ukraine in violation of Article 2, paragraph 4, of the Charter of the United Nations;".
Replace with: "Calls upon all parties to immediately cease hostilities and to engage in dialogue aimed at a peaceful settlement in accordance with the Minsk agreements and the Normandy Format."
Retain only if made applicable to all parties and without implying fault by the Russian Federation; add reference to the need to respect the rights of all civilians in Ukraine.
Delete the paragraph reaffirming Ukraine's territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders.

United Arab Emirates.change: Add: “Calls for an immediate cessation of hostilities and the resumption of diplomatic negotiations aimed at a peaceful resolution and de-escalation, with full respect for the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Ukraine;”
Replace with: “Condemns the use of force against Ukraine in violation of Article 2, paragraph 4, of the Charter of the United Nations and calls upon all parties to exercise maximum restraint;”

Replace with: “Calls upon all parties to respect international humanitarian law and human rights law, to protect civilians, and to ensure safe, unhindered and non-discriminatory access to humanitarian assistance for those in need;”

messages.Brazil: Brazil supports the current draft and will vote in favour. We urge all parties to cease hostilities immediately, protect civilians and ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access. Brazil also calls for a return to diplomatic dialogue and a peaceful settlement consistent with the UN Charter.
messages.China: China’s consistent position is that the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all countries should be respected, while the legitimate security concerns of all parties should also be taken seriously. The current text is one-sided in condemning and naming only one party, and it does not reflect the need for dialogue and a political settlement. China therefore cannot support the draft as drafted and will abstain if it is put to the vote unchanged. We propose these amendments to restore balance and create conditions for de-escalation and negotiations.
messages.France: France fully supports the draft as circulated and is proud to co-sponsor it. The Council must speak clearly and without delay in response to the Russian Federation's aggression against Ukraine and demand the immediate, complete and unconditional withdrawal of its forces. We call on all members to support the text and on the Russian Federation to uphold its Charter obligations rather than block the Council.
messages.Gabon: Gabon supports the current draft and commends the penholder for a text firmly grounded in the Charter’s principles of sovereignty and territorial integrity. We call for the immediate cessation of hostilities and full respect for international humanitarian law, and we see no need for changes at this stage. Gabon is ready to vote in favour and urges the Council to speak with one voice.
messages.Ghana: Ghana supports the draft as circulated. We believe the Council must speak clearly in defence of the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Ukraine and against the use of force in violation of the Charter. Ghana urges all parties to cease hostilities and ensure safe humanitarian access, and calls on Council members to unite behind this text.
messages.India: India remains deeply concerned by the escalating situation and its humanitarian impact, including on Indian nationals. We cannot support language that singles out and condemns one party; the Council should call for an immediate cessation of hostilities, de-escalation and a return to dialogue and diplomacy. With the amendments above India could support the text; absent them, India would abstain.
messages.Ireland: Ireland, as a co-sponsor, fully supports the draft text as circulated. It clearly reaffirms Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and demands that the Russian Federation cease its use of force and withdraw its forces. We urge the penholder to move swiftly to a vote and call on all Council members to uphold the Charter.
messages.Kenya: Kenya supports the draft resolution as circulated. Our position is grounded in the Charter’s prohibition on the use of force and in respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all States, including Ukraine. We urge the Council to speak with one voice and to keep humanitarian access and peaceful settlement at the centre of its response.
messages.Mexico: Mexico supports the draft as circulated. We strongly condemn the Russian Federation’s aggression against Ukraine and reaffirm Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders. We urge the immediate cessation of hostilities, the unconditional withdrawal of Russian forces, and guaranteed humanitarian access and protection of civilians. Mexico remains committed to peaceful settlement through dialogue, but we do not propose amendments at this stage.
messages.Norway: Norway fully supports the draft as circulated and is proud to co-sponsor it. The text rightly condemns the Russian Federation’s aggression against Ukraine and demands an immediate, complete and unconditional withdrawal of its military forces. We urge the penholder to move swiftly to a vote and call on all Council members to support the draft.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation cannot support a text that brands our actions as aggression, demands the withdrawal of our forces, and disputes the territorial realities that have emerged since 2014. These are unacceptable red lines, and Russia will vote against the draft if they remain. If the penholder seeks a balanced text, it must remove the condemnations and demands directed against the Russian Federation and call on all parties to cease hostilities and return to the Minsk agreements.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The UAE supports the draft’s reaffirmation of Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and its humanitarian provisions, but as currently drafted we would abstain. To enable us to support the text, we ask for an explicit call for an immediate cessation of hostilities and the resumption of diplomatic negotiations, and we prefer that the condemnation be framed in terms of the use of force and Charter violations rather than a political attribution. We also seek clear language on protection of civilians and non-discriminatory humanitarian access.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom fully supports this draft and is pleased to co-sponsor it. We see no need for changes and urge the penholder to put it to a vote without delay. Any attempt to weaken the text, including on Ukraine's territorial integrity or the demand for Russian withdrawal, would be unacceptable. Russia must immediately cease its aggression and withdraw its forces.
messages.United States of America: The United States is a co-sponsor of this draft and fully supports it as written. The text directly addresses the Russian Federation’s aggression against Ukraine and demands the immediate cessation of hostilities and withdrawal of Russian forces. We urge the Council to move to a vote without delay and to speak with one voice in defense of the Charter and Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.

replies.United Arab Emirates: rejected: proposed changes would weaken the clear condemnation and demand for withdrawal, even if some humanitarian language is constructive

steps.summary: The draft remains unchanged because the core provisions condemning Russian aggression and demanding full withdrawal are essential to Albania's position and the Charter. Amendments proposed by Russia, China, India and the UAE would dilute or remove that clear message, and the penholder therefore rejects them. The expected vote reflects broad support for the text, with Russia voting against and China, India and the UAE abstaining.

messages.Brazil: Brazil supports the draft as it stands and will vote in favour. The text appropriately reaffirms Ukraine's sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity and calls for unhindered humanitarian access. We urge all parties to cease hostilities and return to dialogue, and we call on Council members to ensure the resolution's adoption.
messages.China: China remains deeply concerned by the deteriorating situation and supports a cessation of hostilities and political dialogue. The current text’s condemnation and demand for withdrawal do not reflect China’s balanced position or the legitimate security concerns of all parties. If these core concerns are not addressed, China will abstain rather than block the Council. We urge the penholder to keep the Council united and avoid language that deepens confrontation.
messages.France: France fully supports the draft as a co-sponsor. The text reflects our red lines: clear condemnation of Russian aggression, an immediate cessation of hostilities and unconditional withdrawal, reaffirmation of Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and respect for international humanitarian law. We urge the penholder to preserve the text’s firmness and move to a vote without dilution.
messages.Gabon: Gabon supports the draft as it stands. It clearly reaffirms Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and calls for an immediate cessation of hostilities and protection of civilians. We urge the Council to remain united and to prioritize humanitarian access and dialogue.
messages.Ghana: Ghana supports the current draft’s reaffirmation of Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity, and its clear demand that the Russian Federation cease its use of force and withdraw its military forces. We also welcome the text’s emphasis on international humanitarian law and safe humanitarian access, and we are prepared to support the draft as presented.
messages.India: India remains deeply concerned by the hostilities and their humanitarian impact, but it cannot support a text that singles out one party for condemnation and demands withdrawal while the Council’s immediate priority should be a cessation of hostilities and a return to dialogue. We therefore reiterate our red-line amendment to OP1 and balanced changes to OP2 and PP4; if these are not reflected, India will abstain. We also ask that OP3 expressly cover the safety and safe passage of foreign nationals, including students.
messages.Ireland: Ireland remains a co-sponsor of this draft and fully supports it as it stands. Given the gravity of the situation following the Russian Federation’s invasion of Ukraine, including reports of attacks on civilian infrastructure and the seizure of Chernobyl, the Council must send an unequivocal message without delay. Ireland urges the penholder to keep the text unchanged and to move promptly to a vote.
messages.Kenya: Kenya supports the draft resolution as it stands. It reflects our consistent position on the sovereignty and territorial integrity of States and the obligation to refrain from the threat or use of force. We urge all parties to cease hostilities immediately and return to dialogue and peaceful settlement. Kenya will vote in favour.
messages.Mexico: Mexico supports the current draft as it stands and will vote in favour. The text clearly condemns the aggression against Ukraine, demands the cessation of force and withdrawal of military forces, and calls for respect for international humanitarian law and humanitarian access. Mexico urges all Council members to unite behind this text.
messages.Norway: Norway remains a co-sponsor and fully supports the draft as currently formulated. We see no need for further changes and urge the Council to proceed to a vote without delay. The text clearly reaffirms Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity and demands an immediate cessation of hostilities and withdrawal of Russian forces. Norway will vote in favour.
messages.Russian Federation: The current text remains unacceptable and we cannot support it. It uses politically charged language against Russia and ignores the root causes of the crisis, including the years-long sabotage of the Minsk agreements. We reiterate that the references to Ukraine's territorial integrity, the “special military operation” and so-called aggression must be removed, and OP2 replaced with a balanced call on all parties to cease hostilities and return to dialogue. If these red lines are not met, we will vote against the draft.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The UAE remains deeply concerned by the escalating violence and humanitarian situation. We reiterate our request for a clear call for an immediate cessation of hostilities and resumption of diplomatic negotiations, as well as balanced language urging all parties to exercise restraint and ensure unhindered humanitarian access. Without these elements, the UAE will abstain on the current text.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the draft as it stands. It clearly condemns the Russian Federation’s aggression against Ukraine, demands an immediate cessation of hostilities and the complete withdrawal of Russian forces, and reaffirms Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. We urge the Council to put this text to the vote without delay and call on all members to vote in favour.
messages.United States of America: The United States fully supports the draft as revised. It clearly condemns the Russian Federation’s aggression against Ukraine and demands the immediate cessation of hostilities and the complete withdrawal of Russian forces from Ukraine’s internationally recognized territory. We urge all Council members to support the text and are ready to proceed to a vote without delay.

reasons.Albania: Albania is strongly pro-Ukraine, pro-EU/NATO, and co-sponsored the resolution, so it would vote in favour and explain its vote before the Council.
reasons.Brazil: Brazil actually voted in favour of this 25 February 2022 UNSC draft condemning Russia’s use of force, while maintaining its diplomatic emphasis on sovereignty, humanitarian access and peaceful settlement. Delivering a pre-vote explanation is consistent with its need to balance support for Ukraine’s territorial integrity with calls for dialogue and restraint.
reasons.China: China abstained on the 25 February 2022 draft resolution, consistent with its opposition to condemnation and forced withdrawal language while urging dialogue. It did not take the floor before the vote.
reasons.France: France is a co-sponsor and has consistently supported Ukraine’s sovereignty and condemned Russian aggression; voting in favour is fully consistent with its policy and alliances. A pre-vote explanation is appropriate to publicly affirm that support and pressure Russia.
reasons.Gabon: Gabon maintained support for the draft in the final negotiation round, reflecting its consistent emphasis on sovereignty, territorial integrity and peaceful settlement of disputes. A yes vote is therefore the appropriate expression of Gabon’s position.
reasons.Ghana: Ghana had already indicated support for the draft, consistent with its foreign policy emphasis on sovereignty, territorial integrity, and peaceful resolution of disputes. As an elected Council member, it would likely explain its affirmative vote publicly.
reasons.India: India abstains to maintain strategic autonomy and a balanced position that avoids condemning Russia while upholding dialogue, sovereignty, and the safety of Indian nationals. The retained core condemnation and withdrawal demands conflict with India's established foreign policy approach.
reasons.Ireland: Ireland is a co-sponsor and firm supporter of Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and would vote in favour of a resolution condemning Russia’s aggression. As an elected Council member with a strong human rights and rules-based order policy, Ireland would explain its vote before the vote.
reasons.Kenya: Kenya consistently defends sovereignty, territorial integrity and peaceful settlement under the UN Charter, and it maintained support for the draft in the last negotiation round. A yes vote is consistent with Kenya’s established foreign policy and its record of condemning violations of Article 2(4).
reasons.Mexico: Mexico’s vote is consistent with its consistent support for Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and its opposition to the use of force under the UN Charter. It speaks to emphasize these principles, call for de-escalation, and highlight the humanitarian imperative.
reasons.Norway: Norway is a co-sponsor and, consistent with its strong support for Ukraine's sovereignty and the UN Charter, would vote yes. As a co-sponsor it would use the opportunity to explain its support before the vote.
reasons.Russian Federation: The draft explicitly condemns Russia's actions and demands withdrawal, directly conflicting with Moscow's position; as a permanent member Russia would vote against and exercise its veto.
reasons.United Arab Emirates: The UAE abstained on the 25 February 2022 UNSC draft condemning Russia’s invasion, favoring de-escalation and diplomatic space while supporting sovereignty and humanitarian language. Its priorities were only partially reflected, and it sought to avoid endorsing a text it viewed as insufficiently balanced.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom is a co-sponsor of the draft and has consistently condemned Russian aggression against Ukraine. It would vote yes and use a pre-vote statement to press for Council unity and Russian withdrawal.
reasons.United States of America: The United States is a co-sponsor of the draft and has consistently supported Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity while opposing Russia’s aggression. It would vote in favor and use a pre-vote statement to press for broad Council support and isolate Russia’s position.

before.Albania: Albania votes in favour of this draft resolution. We co-sponsored it because the Security Council must speak clearly and responsibly in the face of Russia’s unprovoked aggression against Ukraine. This is a grave violation of the Charter, in particular Article 2, paragraph 4, and of Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. We demand that the Russian Federation immediately cease its use of force and unconditionally withdraw its military forces from the territory of Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders. We call on all parties to protect civilians, respect international humanitarian law, and return immediately to diplomacy. Albania will continue to stand with the people of Ukraine and with the principles upon which this Council is founded.
before.Brazil: Brazil will vote in favour of this draft resolution. Our vote reflects Brazil’s firm commitment to the Charter of the United Nations, particularly the sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of States and the peaceful settlement of disputes. Brazil condemns the use of force and calls for an immediate cessation of hostilities, full respect for international humanitarian law, protection of civilians and unhindered humanitarian access. We urge all parties to exercise maximum restraint, to de-escalate and to return to diplomatic negotiations. Brazil is not taking sides in any geopolitical confrontation; we are on the side of peace, dialogue and the rule of law. We stand ready to contribute to a peaceful solution.
before.France: France will vote in favour of this draft resolution. France condemns in the strongest possible terms the Russian Federation’s armed aggression against Ukraine, a flagrant violation of the Charter of the United Nations and of Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders. We demand that Russia immediately cease its use of force and withdraw all its military forces from Ukrainian territory. France remains fully committed to the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Ukraine and to the protection of civilians and unhindered humanitarian access. The Council must shoulder its responsibilities; this text expresses the minimum required by the Charter and by the international community.
before.Gabon: Gabon votes in favour of this draft resolution. We reaffirm our attachment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders. We call for an immediate cessation of hostilities, respect for international humanitarian law, protection of civilians and safe humanitarian access. We urge all parties to return to dialogue and to pursue a peaceful resolution of the crisis.
before.Ghana: Ghana votes in favour of this draft resolution. Our position is guided by the fundamental principles of the Charter of the United Nations, in particular respect for the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of all States and the obligation to refrain from the threat or use of force. Ghana condemns the military operations in Ukraine, calls for an immediate cessation of hostilities, and urges the Russian Federation to withdraw its forces and return to dialogue and peaceful settlement. We also call for the protection of civilians and safe, unhindered humanitarian access. Ghana remains committed to diplomacy and to the territorial integrity of Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders.
before.India: Thank you, Mr. President. India is deeply concerned at the deteriorating situation in Ukraine. We are particularly concerned about the safety and security of Indian nationals, including a large number of students, stranded in Ukraine. We have been in touch with both Russia and Ukraine and have conveyed our strong interest in ensuring the safety and security of our nationals. We call for safe and secure humanitarian access to those in need, including the safe passage of civilians and foreign nationals. India has always stood for peaceful resolution of disputes through dialogue and diplomacy. We believe that the situation can only be resolved through negotiations. We therefore call for an immediate cessation of hostilities and a return to the path of dialogue and diplomacy. We urge all parties to exercise restraint and to respect international law, the UN Charter, and the sovereignty and territorial integrity of states. India is ready to contribute to all efforts aimed at a peaceful resolution. With these considerations, India will abstain on the draft resolution before us.
before.Ireland: Thank you, President. Ireland votes in favour of this resolution. We do so because the Council must be clear and unequivocal in the face of Russia’s unprovoked and unjustified aggression against Ukraine. This is a flagrant violation of the Charter of the United Nations and of Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity within its internationally recognised borders. Ireland demands that the Russian Federation immediately cease its use of force and completely and unconditionally withdraw its military forces from Ukraine. We call for an immediate cessation of hostilities, for maximum restraint by all parties, for the protection of civilians, and for safe, unhindered and non-discriminatory humanitarian access. The Council has a responsibility to uphold the Charter and to stand with the Ukrainian people at this grave moment. Ireland will continue to support every effort towards a peaceful resolution, accountability and respect for international law.
before.Kenya: Mr. President, Kenya votes in favour of this draft resolution because we remain firmly committed to the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations, including the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of all States within their internationally recognized borders. We are gravely concerned by the escalation of hostilities in Ukraine, which poses a serious threat to international peace and security. The use of force against the territorial integrity or political independence of any State is incompatible with Article 2, paragraph 4, of the Charter. Kenya therefore supports the call for the immediate cessation of hostilities, the withdrawal of military forces, respect for international humanitarian law, protection of civilians, and a return to diplomacy and peaceful settlement. We urge all parties to prioritize dialogue and de-escalation and to uphold the Charter, which remains our common safeguard against the return of domination and coercion in international relations.
before.Mexico: Mexico votes in favour of this draft resolution because it upholds the fundamental principles of the Charter of the United Nations: the sovereignty and territorial integrity of States, the non-use of force, and the peaceful settlement of disputes. My delegation condemns the military action against Ukraine and calls for the immediate cessation of hostilities and the withdrawal of forces. At the same time, we urge all parties to protect civilians, guarantee humanitarian access, and return to diplomacy and dialogue as the only viable path to peace.
before.Norway: Norway votes in favour of this resolution. We strongly condemn the Russian Federation's aggression against Ukraine, which is a grave violation of the Charter of the United Nations and of Ukraine's sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. Norway calls on the Russian Federation to immediately cease its use of force and completely and unconditionally withdraw its military forces from Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders. We also call for full respect for international humanitarian law and for safe, unhindered humanitarian access to all those in need. Norway remains firmly committed to diplomacy and to a peaceful resolution of this conflict, with full respect for Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity.
before.Russian Federation: Господин Председатель, представленный на голосование проект резолюции является несбалансированным и политизированным. Он игнорирует коренные причины нынешнего кризиса, включая многолетние преступления киевского режима против жителей Донбасса, и пытается возложить всю ответственность на Российскую Федерацию. Российская Федерация неоднократно заявляла, что происходящее является вынужденной мерой, продиктованной необходимостью защиты населения Донбасса и обеспечения безопасности нашей страны в соответствии со статьёй 51 Устава Организации Объединённых Наций. Мы не можем поддержать документ, основанный на ложных обвинениях и не учитывающий реальные озабоченности России. Призываем все стороны к прекращению огня и переговорам, однако данный проект в нынешнем виде этому не способствует. Российская Федерация голосует против.
before.United Arab Emirates:
Mr. President,

The United Arab Emirates remains gravely concerned by the deteriorating situation in Ukraine and by the humanitarian impact on civilians. We have consistently called for an immediate cessation of hostilities, respect for the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Ukraine, the protection of civilians, and a return to diplomatic negotiations.

While the draft before us contains important elements in this regard, it does not, in our view, fully preserve the balance and Council unity needed to create space for diplomacy and de-escalation. For that reason, the United Arab Emirates will abstain on this draft resolution. We remain committed to working with all Council members and the wider international community to support a peaceful resolution.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom fully supports this draft resolution and will vote in favour. The Russian Federation has launched an unprovoked and unjustified attack on Ukraine, in flagrant violation of the Charter of the United Nations and of Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. We condemn in the strongest terms Russia’s aggression, including attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure and the reckless seizure of Chernobyl. We demand that Russia immediately cease its use of force and withdraw all of its military forces from Ukraine within its internationally recognised borders. This Council must speak with one voice, and the United Kingdom urges all members to support this resolution.
before.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States strongly supports this draft resolution. It does exactly what this Council must do in the face of an unprovoked and unjustified attack on a sovereign Member State: condemn the Russian Federation’s aggression, demand an immediate cessation of hostilities, and require the complete withdrawal of Russian forces from Ukraine’s internationally recognized borders. The Charter is not optional, and this Council cannot remain silent while a permanent member wages war against its neighbor. We call on every member of this Council to vote in favor. The world is watching, and history will judge where we stood. Thank you.

after.Albania: Thank you, Mr. President. Albania deeply regrets that this Council has been prevented from discharging its primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security by the negative vote of the very permanent member that is committing aggression against its neighbour. Eleven members voted in favour of a clear, principled and balanced text; only one voted against. That isolation speaks for itself. The use of the veto cannot confer legitimacy on the use of force or override the Charter. The Security Council has failed today to adopt this resolution, but it has not changed the facts: Russia’s aggression against Ukraine is a flagrant violation of international law and of Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. Albania will continue to stand with Ukraine and with all those who defend the Charter. We demand once again that the Russian Federation immediately cease its use of force and completely and unconditionally withdraw its military forces from the territory of Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders. We call for an immediate cessation of hostilities, protection of civilians, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and a return to genuine diplomacy. Albania will not accept that the veto can silence this Council. Thank you.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China abstained on the draft resolution just put to the vote. China’s position on the Ukraine issue is consistent and clear. We have always advocated respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all countries and the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations. We believe that disputes should be resolved peacefully through dialogue and negotiation.

The current situation in Ukraine has been caused by complex historical and contemporary factors. China is deeply concerned about the latest developments. We call on all parties to exercise restraint, avoid further escalation, and return to political dialogue. We welcome the willingness of Russia and Ukraine to engage in negotiations and support all efforts conducive to a peaceful settlement.

We believe that the security of one country cannot be achieved at the expense of the security of others, and regional security cannot be guaranteed by expanding military alliances. The Cold War mentality should be abandoned, and a balanced, effective and sustainable European security architecture should be established through dialogue and negotiation.

The draft resolution did not fully reflect the complexity of the situation and the legitimate security concerns of all parties, nor did it give sufficient emphasis to resolving the crisis through dialogue and diplomacy. That is why China abstained. China will continue to play a constructive role in promoting a peaceful settlement and in easing the humanitarian situation. All parties should protect the safety of civilians, including foreign nationals. Thank you.
after.France:
Mr. President,

France voted in favour of this draft resolution, and it regrets that the Security Council has been prevented from adopting it by the veto of the Russian Federation. A permanent member has used its veto to shield its own aggression against Ukraine. That veto does not confer legitimacy on the use of force; it isolates Russia still further before the international community.

France condemns in the strongest possible terms the Russian Federation’s armed aggression against Ukraine, a flagrant violation of the Charter of the United Nations and of Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders. France demands that Russia immediately cease its use of force and completely withdraw its military forces from Ukrainian territory.

The failure of this Council to act does not diminish the obligations of the Russian Federation under the Charter, nor does it weaken our determination. France will continue to stand with the Ukrainian people and to work with its partners to protect civilians, ensure humanitarian access, support Ukraine, and oppose this aggression. The Security Council must not remain silent, and France will not abandon its responsibilities.
after.India: Mr. President, India abstains on this resolution. We are deeply concerned at the deteriorating situation in Ukraine. We are particularly concerned about the safety and security of Indian nationals, including a large number of students, stranded in Ukraine. We have been in touch with both Russia and Ukraine and have conveyed our strong interest in ensuring the safety and security of our nationals. We call for safe and secure humanitarian access to those in need, including the safe passage of civilians and foreign nationals. India has always stood for peaceful resolution of disputes through dialogue and diplomacy. We believe that the situation can only be resolved through negotiations. We therefore call for an immediate cessation of hostilities and a return to the path of dialogue and diplomacy. We urge all parties to exercise restraint and to respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all States. We remain committed to the peaceful resolution of the situation.
after.Ireland:
Thank you, Mr. President.

Ireland voted in favour of this resolution because it set out the minimum that this Council should be able to say in the face of an unprovoked and unjustified act of aggression against a sovereign Member State. We deeply regret that the Council has been prevented from adopting it by the negative vote of the Russian Federation.

That veto does not alter the facts. Russia’s use of force against Ukraine is a flagrant violation of the Charter of the United Nations and of Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity within its internationally recognised borders. Ireland again demands that the Russian Federation immediately cease its use of force and completely and unconditionally withdraw its military forces from Ukraine. We call for an immediate cessation of hostilities, for the protection of civilians, and for safe, unhindered and non-discriminatory humanitarian access.

The Council has been prevented from acting today. That does not release the wider membership of the United Nations from its responsibilities. Ireland will work with partners to ensure that the voice of the General Assembly is heard clearly in defence of the Charter and of Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. We stand with the people of Ukraine.

Thank you.
after.Mexico: Mr. President, Mexico voted in favour of the draft resolution because it upholds the principles of the Charter: the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Ukraine; the prohibition of the use or threat of force; and the peaceful settlement of disputes. We deeply regret that the Security Council has been unable to adopt it because of the veto of a permanent member. Mexico has consistently held that the veto cannot be a licence to ignore the Charter. Together with France, we have promoted the suspension of the veto in cases of mass atrocities. The current hostilities have grave humanitarian consequences. We reiterate our call for an immediate cessation of hostilities, the withdrawal of all military forces, full respect for international humanitarian law, and safe, unhindered and non-discriminatory humanitarian access. Mexico will continue to support dialogue and diplomacy as the only way to achieve a peaceful solution that preserves Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. The Council must uphold its responsibilities and the Charter.
after.Russian Federation: Господин Председатель, Российская Федерация уже изложила причины, по которым не могла поддержать данный проект. Добавлю лишь, что звучащие здесь обвинения в адрес нашей страны беспочвенны. Россия действует в соответствии со статьёй 51 Устава ООН, вынужденно, в целях защиты населения Донбасса и обеспечения собственной безопасности. Мы не планируем оккупировать Украину и не наносим удары по гражданским объектам. Применение права вето — это законный инструмент, предусмотренный Уставом, и мы используем его для предотвращения попыток протащить односторонние политизированные решения. Мы остаёмся открытыми для переговоров, но не принимаем попыток говорить с Россией с позиции силы и диктовать ей условия. Призываем наших коллег прекратить нагнетать напряжённость и вернуться к реальной дипломатии. Благодарю.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Mr President,

The United Kingdom voted in favour of this resolution, and we deeply regret that it has been vetoed by the Russian Federation. This was not a complicated text. It reaffirmed the Charter. It upheld Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. It demanded that Russia stop its unprovoked and unjustified attack and withdraw its forces from Ukraine.

Russia’s veto cannot make aggression lawful. It cannot erase Russia’s obligations under the United Nations Charter. It cannot silence the facts: Russia has launched a war of choice against Ukraine, is attacking cities and civilians, and has recklessly seized the Chernobyl nuclear site, threatening the safety of all of Europe.

The result today is clear: eleven members voted in favour, and only one member — the aggressor itself — voted against. Russia stands isolated. The United Kingdom will not accept impunity or the rewriting of the Charter. We will continue to support Ukraine, work with partners to hold Russia accountable, and ensure that the international community does not fall silent in the face of this aggression. We call on Russia once again to cease its military operations immediately and completely withdraw its forces from the territory of Ukraine within its internationally recognised borders.

Thank you.
after.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States is outraged that the Russian Federation has used its veto to block a resolution that merely restated the Charter’s most basic obligations: respect sovereignty, refrain from the threat or use of force, protect civilians, and withdraw military forces. This veto is a badge of shame. It does not change the facts. Russia is the aggressor; Ukraine is the victim. Russia’s attack is unprovoked, unjustified, and a flagrant violation of international law and the United Nations Charter. We thank the eleven members who voted in favor of this resolution. Let me be clear to our Russian colleagues: you can veto this resolution, but you cannot veto the truth. You cannot veto the Ukrainian people. You cannot veto the Charter or this Council’s responsibility. The United States will not be deterred. We will continue to stand with Ukraine and its sovereignty and territorial integrity. We will work with allies and partners to impose severe consequences, press for an immediate cessation of hostilities and safe humanitarian access, and pursue accountability for violations of international law. We will also take this issue to the General Assembly, where every Member State will have the opportunity to speak clearly. The world is watching, and history will judge where we stood. Thank you.
